headline: Deemed dogs at four addresses nuisance or dangerous and set owner conditions; dismissed one dangerous dog hearing.
summary: Six dog cases were heard. Dogs at four addresses were labeled nuisance or dangerous, and each owner received conditions such as humane restraint and confinement. A dangerous dog hearing for Sir Michael at 9 Kensington Ave. was dismissed after the animal control officer asked to withdraw it.
decisions: Approved minutes of the July 16, 2026 meeting, 4-0.
Deemed Zoro and Choloe nuisance dogs, 4-0.
Imposed three conditions on Zoro and Choloe, including humane restraint and confinement to the owner's premises, 4-0.
Deemed Onyx and Junior dangerous dogs, 4-0.
Imposed conditions on Onyx and Junior, including fence upkeep and muzzling off the property, 4-0.
Deemed Angelo and Babble nuisance dogs, 4-0.
Imposed three conditions on Angelo and Babble, including confinement to 106 Edgemont Street, 4-0.
Deemed Ryder and Bluejay nuisance dogs, 4-0.
Imposed three conditions on Ryder and Bluejay, including humane restraint and use of the kennel, 4-0.
Dismissed the dangerous dog hearing for Sir Michael at 9 Kensington Ave., 4-0, after the animal control officer asked to withdraw it.

plain_text:
Animal Control Hearing  
                                                              Minutes 
Call to Order 
10:00 AM Meeting called to order on Thursday, October 15, 2026 at City Hall -- Room 
205, 36 Court Street, Springfield, MA. 
 
Attendee Name Title Status Arrived 
Melvin A. Edwards Ward 3 Councilor Present  
Keith Fleming Police  Present  
Camile Nelson Campbell Assistant City Clerk Present  
Megan Landry Board Member Present  
Veronica Johns Board Member Absent  
Approval of Minutes 
1. July 16, 2026 Minutes 
Read. 
Board Member Landry made a motion to accept the minutes the motion was 
seconded by Board Member Edwards. 
 
Roll call votes on the motion 
 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns     Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell yes 
 
Motion passed by roll call votes. 
 
Minutes approved. 
Dog Hearing 
2. A Nuisance Dog Hearing for two dogs named Zoro and Chole Owned by Michael 
Amoah at 57 Forest Park Ave. 
 
Read.  
Complainant
Aida Alvarado stated she lives there for the past seven to eight years. The dogs would come in her yard, 
and she had arguments with the owner about his dogs coming in her yard, she yelled at him, stating she 
doesn’t want his pit bulls in her yard. She has pictures of the owner in her backyard trying to get his 
dogs. She stated that the two dogs came up to her porch and she started screaming and the owner 
started to laugh. She doesn’t think it's funny, she should not feel like they’re prisoners of their own 
home. This is an ongoing situation where she has called the police on various times, and the MSPCA who 
came out on several time. She doesn’t know what else can be done. She wants something to be done. 
Respondent 
Michael Amoah did not appear. 
Rebuttal 
None 
Renee Robichaud and Elfred Mateo, Animal Control Officer for Thomas J. O’Connor (TJO) 
and Adoption Center read their reports.  
Board Member Edwards made a motion to deem the dogs named Zoro and Choloe 
nuisance dogs the motion was seconded by Board Member Landry. 
 
Roll call votes on the motion 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Motion passed by roll call votes. 
After review of the hearing testimonies and the Thomas J. O’Connor Animal 
Control and Adoption Center reports, the Committee has imposed the following 
conditions on Zoro and Choloe: 
 
1. 1 That the dogs be humanely restrained, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(1) of the Code; 
2. That the dogs be confined to the premises of the owner; provided, however, that "confined" 
shall mean securely confined indoors or confined outdoors in a securely enclosed and locked 
pen or dog run area upon the premises of the owner; provided however, that such 
confinement shall comply with § 110-8 of the Code, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(2) of 
the Code;
3. That the dogs be license, neutered, spayed and registered, in accordance with c. 110 § 
10(B)(9) of the Code. 
Roll call votes on the conditions 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Conditions passed by roll call votes. 
3. A Dangerous Dog Hearing for two dogs named Onyx and Junior Owned by Phoebe 
Kirkpatrick at 179 Ashland Ave. 
Read.  
 
Complainant   
Kayleen Whitaker stated her neighbor’s dogs broke through her fence and killed her Aussie 
Doodle puppy. On April 9, 2026 she spoke to Phoebe and state her concerns about the dogs 
in her yard, she said she would take steps to block the opening and keep closer eye on her 
dogs to make sure it doesn’t happen again. On august 14, 2016 the dogs broke through the 
fence again, entered her backyard and killed her puppy. Phoebe knew her dogs could get in 
her yard and she assured her, that she would watch her dogs more closely, yet it happened 
again. Since that day she has been afraid to go into her backyard. She has two children, a 
3-year-old and a 6-year-old. She’s scared for their safety, she worried about what could 
happen if those dogs get through the fence again. Loosing her dog has really, really 
devasting to her family. She’s afraid that another dog, her children or someone else could 
be hurt in the future. The Dogs are very aggressive. They haven’t really been outside since 
for more than an hour because they are afraid that the dogs will find a way to their 
backyard.  
Respondent 
Phoebe Kirkpatrick stated it is unfortunate that her dog died, it is unfounded that her 
animals had anything to do with it. The complaint is entirely unfounded, retaliatory, and 
lacks any supporting evidence. She has submitted insurance, videos and pictures, that 
proves her dogs are fully compliant, properly licensed, and securely contained, and that no 
provoked physical harm ever occurred. The first incident in April, one of her animals did dig 
underneath the fence and they did repair it. The dogs did not touch the fence for 4 months 
until the day she called her. It was a nice day, her kids were playing and her dogs were 
outside, and she called her afterwards telling her something had happened. She honestly 
doesn’t know what happened to her dog, but her dogs did not look like they got into a fight. 
There was no blood on her animals or furs anywhere. They put up another fence. She has 
letters from neighbors. She deeply saddens of her dog death, there’s no proof that her 
animals cause the death of her dog.
Rebuttal 
Kayleen said when it happened, Phoebe was in tears and apologizing and offered to cremate 
her dog. She has photos and videos of her dog in Phoebe dog’s mouth. Phoebe made a 
promise once and she did not follow through with it. Phoebe took her dog and disposed of 
him somewhere because she was in so much tears and did not want to see her dog like 
that. She doesn’t where they took him. 
Phoebe said she did not make any promises, but she has contained her fence and backyard. 
Her dogs never had any instances or issues previous to this, and will not continue, her dogs 
do not get out. It is unfortunate that her animal pass away. 
 
None 
Renee Robichaud, Animal Control Officer for Thomas J. O’Connor (TJO) and Adoption Center 
read their reports.  
Board Member Fleming made a motion to deem the dogs named Onyx and Junior 
dangerous dogs the motion was seconded by Board Member Edwards. 
 
Roll call votes on the motion 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Motion passed by roll call votes. 
After review of the hearing testimonies and the Thomas J. O’Connor Animal 
Control and Adoption Center reports, the Committee has imposed the following 
conditions on Onyx and Junior: 
1. That the owner of the dogs maintained the fence; in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(9) of the 
Code. 
2. That the dogs be muzzled whenever off the property, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(3) of 
the Code; 
3. That ownership of the dog(s) may not be transferred unless the transfer of ownership is to an 
adult residing within the same residence and the dog(s) shall remain housed solely at that 
residence, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(6) of the Code; 
Roll call votes on the conditions
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
4. A Nuisance Dog Hearing for two dogs named Angelo and Babble Owned by Johana 
Jimenez at 106 Edgemont St. 
Read.  
 
Complainant   
DawnMarie stated there’s two dogs that gets out all the time, she specially had them videos 
and pictures on February 17, 2026, July 2,2026, august 13, 2026, august 14 2026, 
September 15 2026, September 24, 2026 and October 6, 2026, that the dates she was able 
take her phone out. She saw them in really, really freezing, like below zero temperatures 
before running around. she very concern about them, she’ worried they are going to get hit 
by a car. The dogs have been out way more times. She tried to communicate with the 
owners a couple of times, but unfortunately, they didn’t seem to understand English, so she 
wasn’t really able to communicate with them. 
Respondent 
Johana Jimenez stated she’s the owner of the dogs. Her house and her ex-husband house 
are together, and he in charge of the dogs because he wanted to keep them. She heard that 
people are complaining about the dogs escaping. She fixed the gate. It is true the dogs 
been getting out; many people have called her. since she fixed the gate, the dogs have not 
been out. Her dogs are not dangerous, it was her who did not fix the gate. 
Rebuttal 
Dawnmarie the last time she saw the dogs was October 6, 2026. She agrees that the dogs 
seem to be good dogs. The own should probably pay attention to contain them so they don’t 
run out the front door.  
Johanna said she will recheck the gate to reassure they can’t cannot get out. 
Renee Robichaud, Animal Control Officer for Thomas J. O’Connor (TJO) and Adoption Center 
read their reports.  
Board Member Edwards made a motion to deem the dogs named Angelo and 
Babble nuisance dogs the motion was seconded by Board Member Landry. 
 
Roll call votes on the motion 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Motion passed by roll call votes. 
After review of the hearing testimonies and the Thomas J. O’Connor Animal 
Control and Adoption Center reports, the Committee has imposed the following 
conditions on Onyx and Junior: 
1. That the dogs be humanely restrained, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(1) of the Code; 
2. That the dogs be confined to the premises of the owner; provided, however, that "confined" 
shall mean securely confined indoors or confined outdoors in a securely enclosed and locked pen 
or dog run area upon the premises of the owner; provided however, that such confinement shall 
comply with § 110-8 of the Code, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(2) of the Code; 
3. That the dogs be confined to 106 Edgemont Street, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(9) of the 
Code. 
Roll call votes on the conditions 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Conditions passed by roll call votes. 
5. A Dangerous Dog Hearing for two dogs named Ryder and Bluejay Owned by 
Crystal Lamb at 27 Riverview St. 
Read.  
 
Complainant   
Frances stated she has concerns about her neighbor dogs. There was a wire fence and the 
dogs would dig under the wire fence and go in her yard and other places. She knocked on 
her neighbor’s door to let them know that their dogs were loosed. She was terrified to go 
into her yard. The neighbor builds a wooden fence and the dogs started making holes in the 
fence. When ever she’s in her backyard the dogs barked profusely. On the day she was 
attacked by the dogs, she came home from work, parked her car and decided to take a look 
at her chimney. I heard the dogs bark, so she quickly stepped back into the boundary, with
the intention of getting to safety in her house. One of the pit bulls burst through the gate a 
lunged towards her and started attacking her. she turned around and swung her back at the 
dog to protect herself. The second Pitt bulls came out of the gate and started to attacking 
her also. The dogs jumped on her stomach, chest and back, as they proceeded to bite her.  
Crystal, her sons and another person came outside and restrained the dog. Her daughter 
called the ambulance, Police and Animal Control. She’s emotionally scarred, she needs her 
life back and safety. The gate is not safe there. She needs protections for herself and her 
family. 
Respondent 
Crystal Lamb stated she took pictures of where Frances was sitting on her property. The 
maintenance person fixed the gate where it was not able to open, but now it’s able to open 
so she’s not sure what happened and how they got out. She asked him how the dog got 
out, he said he forgot to close the gate. 
Thomas Smith, Jr stated they were watching TV and playing games when they heard 
screaming. They went outside and saw Frances on the ground and the dogs next to her. Hi 
brother grabbed Blue Jay and he grabbed Ryder. 
Alton Alanos stated he heard screaming and went outside and when he looked at the corner 
the gate was open. He always checks the gate, because there’s a latch on the top a bottom. 
Blued Jay was on the right side of the house, all the dogs were on their property. The dogs 
weren’t biting her.  
Rebuttal 
Frances said, they are blaming the contractor for opening the gate. She always has 
concerns about the dogs. She has papers from her doctor. She still has issues with under 
her arm with the lymph nodes. She’s so afraid and she traumatized. She was not 
trespassing. The issued is that they did not take enough care of those ferocious dogs. The 
dogs were on her chest. The dog bit her. The dogs are vicious and dangerous dogs. She has 
doctor’s report and emergency report, tetanus shot. A damaged shoulder, constant pain and 
emotional scar. They didn’t take responsibility for their dogs. 
Alton said they don’t knock against the fence. There are raccoons and skunks in their yard 
constantly. Francis has cats always walking on top of the fence. That’s is the reason they 
are constantly barking. The dogs don’t have any bite records. 
Crystal said her dogs are not vicious, they were nuisance in the past, but they are not 
nuisance now. She’s not saying her dogs didn’t get out, yes, they got out on their property 
and it’s just unfortunate that this happened. she fell and the dogs scratched her. 
 
Renee Robichaud, Animal Control Officer for Thomas J. O’Connor (TJO) and Adoption Center 
read their reports.  
Board Member Edwards made a motion to deem the dogs named Ryder and 
Bluejay nuisance dogs the motion was seconded by Board Member Nelson 
Campbell. 
 
Roll call votes on the motion
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Motion passed by roll call votes. 
After review of the hearing testimonies and the Thomas J. O’Connor Animal 
Control and Adoption Center reports, the Committee has imposed the following 
conditions on Onyx and Junior: 
1. That the dogs be humanely restrained, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(1) of the Code; 
2. That the dogs be confined to the premises of the owner; provided, however, that "confined" 
shall mean securely confined indoors or confined outdoors in a securely enclosed and locked pen 
or dog run area upon the premises of the owner; provided however, that such confinement shall 
comply with § 110-8 of the Code, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(2) of the Code; 
3. That the owner utilized the kennel, in accordance with c. 110 § 10(B)(9) of the Code 
 
Roll call votes on the conditions 
Board member Edwards  Yes  
Board member Fleming  Yes 
Board member Johns   Absent 
Board member Landry  Yes 
Board member Nelson Campbell Yes 
 
Conditions passed by roll call votes.

Read.  
 
Complainant

None
